rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Prompts live in registry; module/exercise/lecture files reference by marker.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Raw source L33 uses {{prompt:ae101-m5-done-done}} correctly, sourcing from `curriculum/prompts/ae101-m5-done-done.md`, with a lead-in above it (content assessed under rule 2).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Disambiguation, anchors, and decision logic that bind Claude live INSIDE prompt fence.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Read the fence in isolation: self-contained, defines 'done-done' within itself, relies only on 'this session'/'this repo' — consistent with its confirmed-warm-session design (maintainer L130: it runs inside the still-live M4 send-off session).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Wide prompts split by logical move — paragraph breaks = cheapest scan-affordance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt is one paragraph (~55 words) with 4 parallel evaluation criteria already visually bracketed by inline '1) 2) 3) 4)' numbering; reads aloud as one breath-group feeding a single 'answer per point' instruction, not the sequential/conditional multi-move shape this rule targets.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Orient saved rule by where it FIRES, not surface activity producing it.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L35: 'putting the definition in ./CLAUDE.md once, where every session reads it and no session has to be told.' — framed by where the rule fires (every future session reading it), not by the activity that produced it (this session's self-audit).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body lead-in mirrors prompt's opening phrasing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body lead-in's last sentence (L31-32) 'Its answer lands in the transcript you are about to read.' beside the prompt's opening 'Are we done-done?' shares no verb or noun-phrase — no phrasal rhyme. Rule 2b's new carve-out exempts the lead-in from needing an action summary at all, but nothing in the compendium extends that exemption to §38's mirroring requirement, and the gap remains real: a student reading the lead-in gets no phrasal echo of what they're about to paste. Harm is mild (the surrounding paragraph at L29 already frames the done-done concept), not severe enough to block ship.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: If the lead-in is ever revised for another reason, end it on a clause that echoes the prompt's opening move, e.g. '...you are about to ask whether the session is done-done.' Not urgent enough on its own to reopen an otherwise-settled, maintainer-reviewed passage.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Declare `permission-mode:` when paste requires specific Claude Code mode.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Registry frontmatter has no `permission-mode:` field, correctly omitted since the prompt's behaviour doesn't depend on plan vs. default mode.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verify session boundary before deciding prompt's context-carrying.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Confirmed WARM via maintainer L130 ('runs in the session you sent off', student pastes into the still-live M4 send-off session). Sub-clause 40b: the prompt self-defines the curriculum-coined term ('done-done') inside the fence rather than assuming the agent already holds it from scrollback.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Output shape — trust Claude's defaults, don't pad.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The per-point shape ('Answer per point, with evidence from this session') is specified because the teaching moment depends on it (maintainer L130: the per-point audit landing in the transcript IS the mechanism), matching the rule's own carve-out for load-bearing shape specification.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Mood contract named.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Maintainer Meta block states the mood target directly: 'learning through contrast', with drift diagnostic and trainer fix recorded (L179). No mechanical/setup beat mistakenly held to the mood-floor; no teaching beat exempted that shouldn't be.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Big Idea (L4) leads with 'Steer your long session', a discipline, not a failure word. Section headers lead with disciplines/insights ('Say what done-done means', 'Inspect your results'); 'Your mid-run worries hint at missing checks' frames the worry as a checks opportunity in the same breath as naming it, not as a bare failure label.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strategy-fidelity check.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No sequencing front-run observed: Ronacher's three-pattern name deliberately withheld until the closing lecture (maintainer Push-back note, L192); 'eval' correctly embargoed to M6 (body uses 'LLM judge', never 'eval'); Cherny withheld from body per the maintainer Frameworks note (L258).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strategic themes recur in Key Concepts.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The four KC bullets (L64-67) instance multiple AE101 themes in the module's own language: baseline/'90%-correct'-adjacent public-field knowledge (L64), capture-your-world specificity via task/model/repo/setup (L65), compounding via candidate-promotion (L66), self-awareness/mirror via the engineer-decides-what-it-means line (L67). Maintainer L140 confirms these four lines are deliberately theme-mapped to the closing lecture's three-pattern slides.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Key Concepts shape — theme breadcrumbs, not standalone section.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No 'Remember:' label, no bold wrapper on any KC bullet — grep clean. Maintainer L140/L147 explicitly locks these four lines verbatim (Antti-decided 2026-08-15, reaffirmed 2026-08-27); the rule's generic breadcrumb expectation is superseded by this documented accept-note.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: What You'll Learn shape — capability register, not syllabus.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All 5 WYL bullets (L15-19) lead with concrete construction/action verbs (Diagnose, Pair, Build, Assemble, Re-send) fitting their objects; no performative/academic verbs, no Bloom-tag parentheticals, no pedagogical-mechanism tails, no author-defence asides, no didactic taxonomy stamps. The colon-based failure-mode-to-packaging pairing (L16) is a concrete artifact list, the licensed carve-out, not a taxonomy stamp.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Self-critique register, not defense, when Claude interrogates own work.
A claim binds to every body that states it, not just the one holding the stamp.
Body "read it" / "look at it" / "notice X" after chat-print = dead weight.
Name the outcome; don't walk a professional through trivial mechanics.
Trust the prompt over the scaffold.
Installed Skills invoke by name, never path.
Chain by back-reference + deterministic path, never invented alias.
Chained-prompt isolation - don't leak downstream pipeline.
No session-resets mid-phase.
Multi-sample methods need structural enforcement.
Runtime-fork prompts: paired divs, shared chip.
Runtime-mechanical scaffolding asymmetry - MORE in less-fluent fork, not less.
Append-vs-integrate - name integration mode on regeneration with new context source.
Citation discipline - extend cite-or-flag scope + quote supporting sentence.
Niceness tax - name the edge or pin the line on regeneration.
Question-dump default - 'in turn' too soft; two legal shapes.
Overwrite anxiety - name overwrite default on regeneration.
Preamble before action - design around it.
Minimal hand-off + Claude self-augments for send-off prompts.
Grill before save - collaborative quality at artefact assembly.
Tell me what you wrote, not show me what you'll write.
Artifact destinations are explicit subpaths, never naked filenames (Agents 101-specific).
Don't restate session CWD inside prompt body.
subagent allowed in prompt blocks; explain why after prompt.
Maintainer-approval edits - ONE-AT-A-TIME, PRIORITY-ORDERED, FOUR-FIELD cards.
Name consumer at write time - 'Save it as <path>' requires downstream reader.
Live-test corrections preserve operator workflow.
Module names in prompt prose are fine - they ground the session.
Git-output greps asserting exact-N need multi-result fallback.
Repeated Q&A -> premature re-edits. Separate iteration from persistence.
Artifact-vs-STOP tail ordering - last imperative wins.
Headless-runner discipline - tail every prompt with no-AUQ guard.
Long-running prompts stream progress - never go silent.
A leading-looking line can be a forcing function; prefer the simpler prompt.
Prompt paths match Builder scope.
"Add X and regenerate" is a trap.
Vary closings deliberately.
CTO-repeatable test.
No stylized phrase-pairs.
Strip strategy-doc vocabulary.
Earn every term.
No M-number cross-references.
"What you build" = 20-30 words.
Describe failure modes, don't name them.
Agency on right noun.
No em dashes on site.
No "What research says" callout boxes.
Don't describe mood arc externally.
Ownership claims scope to customer-built artifacts.
Numbers carry their denominator + axis.
Epistemic mood != punitive mood.
Rough-cut drafts for articles.
Verbatim-frame-cite in reference artefact.
The `**What happened:**` block is OPTIONAL — default is to omit it.
A rule set reconstructed at session start goes stale inside the session — re-derive it per target, not per sweep.
One doc per scarce-attention audience; delta-only.
Trainer-facing text is self-contained.
Business-audience word ban (Agents 101 default).
Q1/Q2/Q3 retro interview is banned at every module.
Simulation personas never alone.
`.md` is default file type for student artifacts across curriculum.
Four sharing strategies (Agents 101 M7 canonical) — use verbatim.
Agents 101 M2+ Debrief — canonical shape.
